indicators.section: Financial Red Flag Indicators of Ransomware and Associated Payments
indicators.flag: A financial institution or its customer detects IT enterprise activity that is connected to ransomware cyber indicators or known cyber threat actors. Malicious cyber activity may be evident in system log files, network traffic, or file information.
indicators.red_flag: IT-enterprise activity linked to ransomware cyber-indicators / known threat actors
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C19 (Adverse-media / OSINT & web-presence verification); data D13.

indicators.section: Financial Red Flag Indicators of Ransomware and Associated Payments
indicators.flag: When opening a new account or during other interactions with the financial institution, a customer provides information that a payment is in response to a ransomware incident.
indicators.red_flag: Customer-stated payment in response to a ransomware incident (onboarding disclosure)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D5 (Transaction narrative / free-text fields), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.section: Financial Red Flag Indicators of Ransomware and Associated Payments
indicators.flag: A customer’s CVC address, or an address with which a customer conducts transactions is connected to ransomware variants,
indicators.red_flag: Counterparty CVC address attributed to ransomware variant / payment activity
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D7 (Virtual-currency / blockchain analytics), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.section: Financial Red Flag Indicators of Ransomware and Associated Payments
indicators.flag: An irregular transaction occurs between an organization, especially an organization from a sector at high risk for targeting by ransomware (e.g., government, financial, educational, healthcare) and a DFIR or CIC, especially one known to facilitate ransomware payments.
indicators.red_flag: High-risk-sector org → DFIR/CIC irregular transfer (ransomware-payment intermediary)
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C1 (Customer-profile / out-of-pattern transaction monitoring); data D1.

indicators.section: Financial Red Flag Indicators of Ransomware and Associated Payments
indicators.flag: A DFIR or CIC customer receives funds from a counterparty and shortly after receipt of funds sends equivalent amounts to a CVC exchange.
indicators.red_flag: Receive-then-forward equivalent to a CVC exchange (DFIR/CIC pass-through)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C2 (Rapid pass-through / flow-through (receive-and-forward) detection).

indicators.section: Financial Red Flag Indicators of Ransomware and Associated Payments
indicators.flag: A customer shows limited knowledge of CVC during onboarding or via other interactions with the financial institution, yet inquires about or purchases CVC (particularly if in a large amount or rush requests), which may indicate the customer is a victim of ransomware.
indicators.red_flag: Low CVC familiarity yet large / rush CVC purchase (ransomware-victim signature)
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C1 (Customer-profile / out-of-pattern transaction monitoring); data D7.

indicators.section: Financial Red Flag Indicators of Ransomware and Associated Payments
indicators.flag: A customer that has no or limited history of CVC transactions sends a large CVC transaction, particularly when outside a company’s normal business practices.
indicators.red_flag: First / out-of-pattern large CVC transfer vs no CVC history
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C6 (Transaction-velocity & dormancy / baseline-deviation monitoring).

indicators.section: Financial Red Flag Indicators of Ransomware and Associated Payments
indicators.flag: A customer that has not identified itself to the CVC exchanger, or registered with FinCEN as a money transmitter, appears to be using the liquidity provided by the exchange to execute large numbers of offsetting transactions between various CVCs, which may indicate that the customer is acting as an unregistered MSB.
indicators.red_flag: Unregistered-MSB pattern: high-volume offsetting cross-CVC trades
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D7 (Virtual-currency / blockchain analytics), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.section: Financial Red Flag Indicators of Ransomware and Associated Payments
indicators.flag: A customer uses a foreign-located CVC exchanger in a high-risk jurisdiction lacking, or known to have inadequate, AML/CFT regulations for CVC entities.
indicators.red_flag: CVC exchanger in high-risk / weak-AML jurisdiction
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C20 (Cross-border / high-risk-jurisdiction & corridor anomaly detection).

indicators.section: Financial Red Flag Indicators of Ransomware and Associated Payments
indicators.flag: A customer receives CVC from an external wallet, and immediately initiates multiple, rapid trades among multiple CVCs, especially AECs, with no apparent related purpose, followed by a transaction off the platform. This may be indicative of attempts to break the chain of custody on the respective blockchains or further obfuscate the transaction.
indicators.red_flag: Rapid multi-CVC / AEC hops then off-platform (chain-of-custody break)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D7 (Virtual-currency / blockchain analytics), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.section: Financial Red Flag Indicators of Ransomware and Associated Payments
indicators.flag: A customer initiates a transfer of funds involving a mixing service.
indicators.red_flag: Transfer routed through a CVC mixing / tumbler service
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D7 (Virtual-currency / blockchain analytics), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.section: Financial Red Flag Indicators of Ransomware and Associated Payments
indicators.flag: A customer uses an encrypted network (e.g., the onion router) or an unidentified web portal to communicate with the recipient of the CVC transaction.
indicators.red_flag: Tor / anonymized-portal contact with the CVC counterparty
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D7 (Virtual-currency / blockchain analytics), not currently held → source data first.
